subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Recovery, Sleep, Hydration, and Injury Prevention
title: Unit assessment: common activity injuries and how they are prevented under transfer
focus: common activity injuries and how they are prevented
essentialQuestion: Why does what I do between sessions decide what happens in them?
privacySafeScenario: Build a recovery protocol for the learner’s own program, including the specific signals that will trigger a reduced or rest day, and a graded return-to-activity plan.
studentTask: Learner works common activity injuries and how they are prevented tracked across a real week that includes at least one bad night or missed session, and adjusted rather than abandoned at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of common activity injuries and how they are prevented degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds common activity injuries and how they are prevented tracked across a real week that includes at least one bad night or missed session, and adjusted rather than abandoned, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing a condition builds the protocol with guardian input around the constraints they already have.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of common activity injuries and how they are prevented yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing a condition builds the protocol with guardian input around the constraints they already have.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where common activity injuries and how they are prevented shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
